item.title: #3591785: Strengthen AutoSaveManager to generate stable hashes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591785 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Drupal Canvas's AutoSaveManager hashes each entity's normalized data both to detect when a draft differs from the last saved version and to detect edit conflicts between concurrent editors. Because that normalization step did not consistently cast values to their canonical PHP types before hashing, equivalent data could produce different hashes, making conflict detection and auto-save comparisons unreliable. This issue strengthens the normalization so hashing is stable and deterministic. On update, a database update hook automatically rehashes all existing stored auto-save entries, so no manual action is required, and the previous fallback that treated entries without a stored hash as conflict-free has been removed since it is no longer needed.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: New canvas_post_update_0026_rehash_auto_save_items() update hook rewrites data, data_hash and original_hash for every existing keyvalue-stored Canvas auto-save entry using the strengthened normalization.

Technical details

The root cause was that AutoSaveManager::toStorableArray() stored raw FieldItemListInterface::getValue() output while normalizeEntity() separately cast primitives via PrimitiveInterface::getCastedValue(), and a near-duplicate casting routine existed in ComponentSourceBase. These divergent, partially-raw code paths meant data_hash computation could differ for logically identical data.

Both are replaced by a single new helper, Drupal\canvas\Utility\TypedDataHelper::castRawPhpTypes(), which recursively normalizes any TypedDataInterface: primitives are cast via getCastedValue(), traversable elements are walked to arrays, an absent value stays NULL while a present-but-empty complex value becomes [], and ComponentTreeItem instances are cloned and run through optimizeInputs() first so equivalent component trees always normalize identically. A few properties are special-cased to keep NULL instead of being cast to '' or 0: ComponentTreeItem::NULLABLE_STRING_PROPERTIES (parent_uuid, slot, label), PathItem::langcode, EntityReferenceItem::target_uuid, and TextItemBase::format. AutoSaveManager::toStorableArray() now also uses this helper, and for config entities carrying a component tree it optimizes inputs on a clone before calling toArray().

With hashing now trustworthy for every entry, the special-case fallback in AutoSaveManager that treated auto-save entries lacking original_hash (from before an earlier commit) as having no conflict was removed from detectConflicts(), resolveConflict(), and getAllAutoSaveList(); the AutoSaveEntry phpstan type now declares original_hash and data_hash as always present. canvas.post_update.php adds canvas_post_update_0026_rehash_auto_save_items(), which uses reflection to invoke the now-private normalizeEntity(), generateHash(), and toStorableArray() methods against every stored auto-save keyvalue entry, rebuilding its data, data_hash, and stored-entity hash in place.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3591905: `drush config:import` can fail to update a Component whose `active_version` changed
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591905 · 1 contributor · 5 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Deploying a Canvas site with drush deploy (or plain drush config:import) could silently fail to update a Component whenever that component's version had changed, for example after adding or removing a prop on a code component. The import would log an error and leave the component at its old version, with no obvious way to tell without checking logs. This particularly affected code components, since the previously known workaround, running a cache rebuild before importing, did not help them: their new configuration only exists in the import itself, so a cache clear just recomputed the old version. This fix makes drush config:import and drush deploy reliably bring Component entities up to date, restoring the expected deploy workflow: edit a component in one environment, export configuration, and import it cleanly in another.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in how Drupal core's config import updates an existing config entity: ConfigEntityStorage::updateFromStorageRecord() copies every exported property from the sync record, including active_version, onto the already-loaded entity object. But VersionedConfigEntityBase::$loadedVersion is derived, non-exported state that is only set once in the constructor. After the property copy, active_version pointed at the new hash while $loadedVersion still pointed at the old one, and VersionedConfigEntityBase::preSave() throws an EntityStorageException whenever those two disagree. ConfigImporter::importInvokeOwner() catches that exception per-object and just logs it, so the import as a whole appeared to succeed while the Component silently stayed on its old version.

The fix adds a new VersionedConfigEntityStorage (extending ConfigEntityStorage) that overrides updateFromStorageRecord() to call $entity->resetToActiveVersion() after the parent copies the record's properties, re-deriving $loadedVersion from the just-updated active_version. Component now declares this as its storage handler directly. A new VersionedConfigEntityHooks::entityTypeAlter() also assigns VersionedConfigEntityStorage automatically to any entity type implementing VersionedConfigEntityInterface that hasn't already customized its storage class, so other versioned config entity types get the same protection without extra wiring. The invariant that a deliberately loaded historical version cannot be saved (even while syncing) is preserved, since resetToActiveVersion() only runs on the property-copy path triggered by config import, not on manual loadVersion() calls.

item.title: #3591851: Allow patterns to be edited
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591851 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Canvas page builder, Patterns (reusable, saved component groupings) could previously only be inserted or deleted. There was no way to fix a mistake or evolve a pattern after it was saved. This adds an "Edit pattern" action that opens the pattern in the full canvas editor, and a "Rename" action for changing its name, both from the pattern's menu in the library panel.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The backend already supported updating a Pattern config entity (Pattern::updateFromClientSide() and the PATCH /canvas/api/v0/config/pattern/{id} route), so the work was mostly building the missing round-trip: loading a stored pattern back into the editor, editing its component tree as a draft, and publishing it back to config, plus wiring up the UI to reach that flow.

New routes canvas.api.layout.get.pattern, .patch.pattern, and .post.pattern (all under /canvas/api/v0/layout-pattern/{entity}) and a dedicated canvas.api.form.component_instance.pattern route give Patterns their own layout/component-instance-form endpoints, since unlike content templates a Pattern renders standalone with no preview entity. ApiLayoutController was generalized to accept ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase (Pattern's base class) alongside ContentTemplate, and AutoSaveManager::entityIsConsideredNew() now treats any ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase as "new" only while unsaved ($entity->isNew()), rather than relying on the default-title heuristic used for content entities. Since a Pattern has no host content entity for field widgets that need entity context (e.g. image or options widgets), Pattern::createEmptyHostEntity() creates a throwaway, unsaved canvas_page to serve that role, mirroring ContentTemplate::createEmptyTargetEntity().

On the frontend, a new /pattern/:patternId route and PatternLayout component fetch and initialize the editor via useGetPatternLayoutQuery, and new postPatternLayout/updateComponentInPattern RTK Query mutations save the draft. PatternItem.tsx gains "Edit pattern" and "Rename" menu entries, the latter opening a new RenamePatternDialog backed by useUpdatePatternMutation (PATCH /canvas/api/v0/config/pattern/{id}). A pattern's name is edited immediately through this config API call, separate from the draft/publish cycle used for its component tree. Topbar and PageInfo were updated to recognize the new EditorFrameContext.PATTERN context, hiding the language selector (patterns aren't translated) and showing the pattern's name in the header.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3591656: Support multi-target-bundle references in code component content-entity-reference props
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591656 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

In Drupal Canvas, code components can declare props that pull data from content entity fields, including fields reached through an entity reference. Until now, if that reference field could point to more than one bundle (for example a "Related content" field that can hold either an Article or a Page), Canvas could not actually render it: the render path threw an explicit error rather than silently producing wrong output, and the Canvas UI's field picker did not let you browse into such a field at all. This issue adds real, end-to-end support: at render time Canvas now resolves the referenced entity first and then picks the correct set of fields for whatever bundle that entity actually turns out to be, and the field picker now lets you browse into a multi-bundle reference field on a per-target-bundle basis. Component authors and site builders no longer need to avoid multi-bundle reference fields when wiring up content-entity-reference props.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

JsComponent::buildReferencePayload() previously threw a \LogicException whenever a reference expression's target was a ReferencedBundleSpecificBranches (the coalesced form produced when a reference field targets multiple bundles, one branch per bundle). It now defers target selection until the referencer resolves to a concrete entity: for each ReferencedBundleSpecificBranches target it calls the new ReferencedBundleSpecificBranches::getBranchForEntityOrNull() to pick the branch matching the resolved entity's entity type and bundle, and for a plain single-bundle target reached through a multi-bundle referencer (an un-coalesced cross-bundle pick) it matches by the target's host entity type and bundle. When nothing matches the resolved entity's bundle, it falls back to a __type-only payload, and cacheability now explicitly includes the traversed entity via addCacheableDependency($entity) since that case has no leaf pick to carry the entity's own cache tags.

On the picker side, ApiUiContentEntityReferenceControllers now offers browsing into a multi-target-bundle reference field, returning one targetBundles entry per bundle. To avoid producing an inexpressible "branch inside a branch" (nested branching, which the string expression format can't yet represent and which the parser rejects), a further multi-bundle descent is withheld once the parent chain already passed through one multi-bundle reference (parentDescendsThroughMultiTargetBundleReference()); that follow-up is tracked in #3591865. The old MultiTargetBundleReferenceNotSupportedConstraint (and its validator) is removed since multi-bundle references are no longer categorically rejected. Two new constraints take its place for the cases still unsupported: EntityFieldExpressionsMustNotNestBranches rejects selections that would coalesce into a nested branch, and EntityFieldExpressionsMustNotMixBundlesInObject rejects picks that read several different fields per bundle across bundles into one object (unrenderable, because each bundle-specific property would throw against the other bundle's entity); mixed-bundle objects becoming a supported branch is tracked in #3591873. A new NestedBranchNotSupportedException lets Coalescer distinguish nested-branch failures from other invalid branch sets, so validation can report the precise "not yet supported" message. The other expression validators (raw-URI, internal-property, multi-valued-field guards) now descend into every branch of a multi-bundle reference instead of skipping it outright, since a violation hidden inside one bundle's branch is still a violation.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 10, 2026

item.title: #3582200: component_tree sequence keys sorted lexicographically instead of numerically, breaking component order at 10+ instances per level
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +40/−6 · php +40/−6
  • Discussion: #3582200 · 1 contributor · 3 comments
  • Followers: 2

Summary

Canvas content templates (and other config entities with a component_tree field) could have their component order silently scrambled once a tree contained 10 or more components at the same level, or once a component's position key had multiple ':'-separated segments (e.g. items nested in a slot). This happened whenever Canvas normalized the stored order, such as on save or config import. A tree stored as 0, 1, 2, ..., 9, 10, 11 would come back as 0, 1, 10, 11, 2, 3, ..., and this corrupted order then propagated to the Canvas layout API and to preview rendering. This fix ensures component order is preserved correctly regardless of how many components a level or slot contains.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was that Canvas encodes a component tree's structure into string keys, such as 4, 4:the_body:0, or 4:the_body:0:<uuid>, and then relies on sorting those keys to recover the intended order. Three call sites, ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::preSave(), and ComponentTreeConfigEntityTransformer::import() and its internal computeExportSequenceKeys(), used PHP's ksort(), which compares keys as plain strings. That makes 10 sort before 2, since lexicographic comparison looks at the first character first.

The fix replaces all three ksort() calls with uksort($tree, \strnatcmp(...)), using PHP's natural-order string comparison so that whole-number segments within the ':'-delimited keys are compared numerically (9 before 10) while still keeping parent keys (4) ordered before their child keys (4:the_body:0). ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::preSave() additionally gained a new componentTreeSequenceIsPositionEncoded() helper, which checks whether the tree's keys are still position-encoded (not yet re-keyed by UUID) so the natural sort is applied only when needed, covering the config install/update path that bypasses the sync import transformer.

Contribution

item.title: #3591820: Publishing a symmetrically-translated canvas_page 422s when a default-language edit changes a non-translatable component input
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591820 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Sites that translate canvas_page entities with content_translation could hit an HTTP 422 error when trying to publish a page after editing a non-translatable ("symmetric") component input, such as an image's width, a section's padding_bottom, or a heading's element (h1 to h6) tag, on a component instance that also exists in another language's translation. The publish would be rejected even though saving the same change directly would have succeeded. This is now fixed: publishing converges the non-default translation's copy of the changed input to match the default translation, and the publish succeeds as expected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was an ordering mismatch between validation and synchronization. content_translation's presave hook is what converges "symmetric" (non-translatable) field columns across a translated entity's translations, but that convergence only happens inside EntityInterface::save(). Canvas's publish path, ApiAutoSaveController::getConflictAwareContentEntityViolations(), validates the entity with $entity->validate() before save() runs, so ComponentTreeSymmetricalTranslationConstraint saw the pre-sync, stale, intermediate state (the auto-save snapshot only ever carries the edited default-language translation) and rejected it.

The fix introduces SymmetricalTranslationSynchronizationTrait, used by both ClientDataToEntityConverter and ApiAutoSaveController. It wraps content_translation.synchronizer (injected as an optional $translationSynchronizer constructor argument, since content_translation is an optional dependency) and exposes synchronizeTranslations()/canSynchronizeTranslations(). getConflictAwareContentEntityViolations() now validates a cloned copy of the entity with translations synchronized, while leaving the entity that is actually saved untouched, so content_translation's presave hook remains the single synchronization pass. This distinction matters because FieldTranslationSynchronizer::synchronizeItems() is not idempotent after a structural edit (an insert or reorder): running it twice on an already-synchronized entity maps inputs to the wrong deltas and corrupts translations. ClientDataToEntityConverter::convert() similarly synchronizes in place before validating, but only on auto-save (never before an actual save()), and only when the entity in hand is the default translation, since a non-default translation being edited is itself a synchronization target and must not be silently overwritten before its own violation can be reported.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">

item.title: #3591857: Removing a media item from one image prop deletes the stored value of every other media-backed prop on the same component instance
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591857 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

In the Canvas page builder, components with more than one image or media prop (for example a component with a "first image" and "second image") had a data-loss bug: clicking the remove (X) button on one image would silently wipe out the other, untouched image prop as well. The saved page and preview would lose the second image even though the editor never touched it. This is now fixed: removing one media item only clears that item, and other media props on the same component instance keep their stored values.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in buildRemoveModel() in ui/src/components/form/components/drupal/DrupalMediaListContainer.tsx. It called syncPropSourcesToResolvedValues() (from layoutModelSlice.ts) across all of a component's props before sending the PATCH to /canvas/api/v0/layout/.... That helper copies each prop's resolved value back into its source.value, but after a prior PATCH round trip the Redux model's resolved value for a media prop is a server-evaluated object ({src, alt, width, height}) rather than a media entity ID. Feeding that evaluated object back as a source.value for the entity-reference-backed StaticPropSource made clientModelToInput() (JsonSchemaPropsComponentSourceBase.php) treat the untouched prop as empty, dropping it from the stored inputs entirely.

The fix narrows buildRemoveModel() to only rewrite the removed prop's source entry (source[propName] = { ...source[propName], value: resolved[propName] }), leaving every other prop's source untouched, and removes the call to syncPropSourcesToResolvedValues() from this code path since it's no longer needed here. The bug was introduced in #3577219; prior remove-path tests only covered single-media-prop components, so the cross-prop corruption wasn't caught. A Playwright regression test was added using the mixed-images-with-example component, populating two image props and removing one, and CanvasMedia.ts's addMediaImage() test helper was extended with an optional fieldset locator so tests can target a specific media widget when a component has multiple media fields.

item.title: #3591716: Boolean props auto-enable when another prop is changed in the Canvas form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591716 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

In the Canvas experience builder, editing a component with boolean properties (for example a "card-program" component) could cause all of its boolean toggle switches to visually flip to ON as soon as any other, unrelated prop was changed, even though the user never touched the toggle. This was purely a display and initial-state bug: it could mislead editors into thinking a boolean prop was enabled when it was not. The fix ensures boolean false values are correctly preserved and displayed as OFF throughout the component editing form, including after AJAX form rebuilds (such as those triggered by media library widgets).

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The input--checkbox--inwidget-boolean-checkbox.html.twig template now reads element[#checked] instead of element[#value] for its current_value variable, and always renders 1 or empty string rather than a raw value.

Technical details

Two distinct bugs combined to produce the symptom. First, in layoutModelSlice.ts, _addNewComponentToLayout's buildInitialData() built a new component's initial prop values using prop.default_values?.resolved || []. Since false || [] evaluates to [] (a truthy value) rather than false, any boolean prop defaulting to false was silently coerced away from its actual value. This was changed to the nullish coalescing operator (?? []), which only falls back to [] when the value is null or undefined, preserving an explicit false. The same || [] to ?? [] fix was applied to the source field.

Second, on the server side, Drupal's Checkbox::valueCallback() returns the integer 0 (not PHP boolean false) for an unchecked checkbox during an AJAX form rebuild. The input--checkbox--inwidget-boolean-checkbox.html.twig template passed element[#value] directly into the current_value attribute consumed by the React DrupalToggle component. Twig rendered the integer 0 as the string "0", and since !!"0" === true in JavaScript, DrupalToggle interpreted this as checked. The template was changed to use element[#checked], a proper boolean set by processCheckbox, and both default_value and current_value are now rendered as either 1 or an empty string, never the ambiguous "0". As a defensive third layer, DrupalToggle.tsx gained a parseChecked() helper that explicitly treats the string "0" and the number 0 as falsy when computing its initial checked state.

Contribution

item.title: #3573022: [upstream] Data loss: `drush config:import` deletes config (e.g. code component + component config entities) and bypasses config system data integrity checks
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3573022 · 3 contributors · 18 comments
  • Followers: 4

Summary

Running drush config:import could silently delete in-use Canvas code components without triggering Canvas's built-in safety mechanisms, leaving dangling references in page content and producing a white screen of death (WSOD) on every page that referenced those components. There was no way to recover without directly editing the database. Canvas now blocks any config import that would delete a component still in use on a page, giving site owners a clear error message and keeping the site intact. Unused components can still be removed via config import.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause is in Drupal core's ConfigImporter::importConfig(), which uses the low-level Config::delete() to remove configuration entries rather than calling ConfigEntityBase::delete(). That bypass means ConfigEntityBase::preDelete() is never invoked, and therefore Component::onDependencyRemoval() never runs. That method is what Canvas relies on to switch an in-use component to its fallback source; without it, deleting a canvas.js_component.* or canvas.component.js.* config entity via drush config:import leaves live page content pointing at configuration that no longer exists.

The fix adds ComponentConfigImportValidator, a final class extending ConfigImportValidateEventSubscriberBase, registered as a service in canvas.services.yml. During ConfigEvents::IMPORT_VALIDATE it inspects the deletion list for two danger vectors: (A) a Component config entity is itself scheduled for deletion, and (B) non-component configuration that a retained Component depends on is being deleted (detected via ConfigManagerInterface::findConfigEntityDependenciesAsEntities()). For every endangered Component the subscriber calls ComponentAudit::hasUsages() for both published revisions and auto-save drafts; if either returns true, the import is aborted via ConfigImporter::logError() with an explanatory message naming the affected component.

This is explicitly a stopgap until core is fixed. The class docblock references two upstream issues: one to route config-import deletions through onDependencyRemoval() and one (#2414951) that would add this class of detection to core itself, at which point the subscriber could be removed rather than just adjusted.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 12, 2026

Key contributors

  • bernardm28
  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • penyaskito (Acquia)
  • phenaproxima (Acquia)

Collaboration

wim leers traced the failure through both Drush and Drupal core source code before any patch existed. He identified that ConfigImporter calls the storage-layer Config::delete() rather than the entity-layer ConfigEntityBase::delete(), which is what bypasses onDependencyRemoval(). He then found Drupal core's content_moderation module using ConfigEvents::IMPORT_VALIDATE for a related-but-different purpose and concluded that the same mechanism was the only mitigation Canvas could apply unilaterally. bernardm28's original report confirmed, in response to wim leers' direct question, that both canvas.js_component.foo and canvas.component.js.foo were wiped together, making the two-vector design of the validator necessary.

item.title: #3591667: Add `canvas:doctor` Drupal CLI command to check health of Canvas' data: validate every Canvas (content|config) entity + translation, validate every non-Canvas content entity component tree field revision+translation, and more
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591667 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The Canvas module now ships a canvas:doctor command (requiring Drupal 11.4's dr CLI) that validates all Canvas data and reports integrity problems. It runs nine distinct health checks: four system checks (Canvas update paths executed, config entities that escaped the update path, whether all installed extensions are at tagged releases, and whether every component source plugin supports schema evolution) and five data checks (Canvas config entities, default content revisions, past revisions, forward/draft revisions, and auto-save snapshots). Each check reports a count of healthy vs. failing items, a duration, and optional per-violation details with a prescription for remediation. The command can output a human-readable table or structured JSON. Validation also runs incrementally via cron on sites that never use the CLI, so health records stay warm without requiring manual intervention.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: New canvas_health_records table is created lazily on first write; no update hook is required.
  • New API: New canvas:doctor CLI command (requires Drupal 11.4+) with --checks, --all-checks, --no-cache, --details, and --format=json options for auditing Canvas data integrity.

Technical details

The implementation is organized into five @internal classes under src/Health/ plus the command itself in src/Command/DoctorCommand.php.

HealthCheck is a string-backed PHP enum with nine cases split into system checks (run once per invocation, never cached) and data checks (streamed as generators, results persisted). The isSystemCheck() and findingsAreRisks() methods are the single source of truth for those splits: adding a new case without updating both exhaustive match expressions causes a PHPStan failure.

Doctor is the validation engine. runDataChecks() yields CheckItem structs via generators, which lets DoctorCommand display a live progress bar without loading all entities into memory first. runCronWindow() accepts an offset and limit, enabling HealthHooks::cron() to advance a cursor stored in Drupal state across separate cron runs. Each data check's freshness signal is computed at the moment Doctor visits the item, not when Inventory listed it, so paginated results from a previous cron run do not carry stale freshness data.

HealthRecords persists results in the canvas_health_records database table (keyed on data_key + check). The table is created lazily on first write rather than via a formal install hook. Freshness is determined by matching two fingerprints: an environment fingerprint (Canvas schema version, count of applied and pending post-updates, xxh64 hash of all installed extension versions) computed by Environment, and a data fingerprint per item (cache-tag checksum for config and content entities, a precomputed data hash for auto-save snapshots). If any installed extension reports no release version (dev), HealthRecords::isFresh() unconditionally returns false, disabling all result reuse.

UpdatesEscapedConfig detection uses reflection to enumerate CanvasConfigUpdater::needs*() methods, filters to those whose first required parameter type-matches the entity being inspected, and calls each. Deprecation emissions from those methods are suppressed during the audit by temporarily calling setDeprecationsEnabled(FALSE). The DoctorCommand itself is thin: it delegates all logic to Doctor so the same validation can power the planned web UI (#3588907 via Drupal Batch API).

item.title: #3591674: Explicitly support `comment` as a referenceable content entity type (stop omitting it from the content entity types endpoint)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591674 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Canvas module, the content entity types API endpoint now correctly lists comment as a referenceable entity type for users who hold access comments and have view access to the parent entity type (e.g., access content for comments on nodes). Previously, comment was silently absent from the picker even when permissions were in place, because the access check always failed on the stub entity used for eligibility testing.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Canvas evaluates whether an entity type/bundle is referenceable by creating an unsaved stub entity and running a 'view' access check on it via getBundleViewAccess(). CommentAccessControlHandler::checkAccess() calls $entity->getCommentedEntity()->access('view'), which throws on a stub that has no commented entity. The error was caught by getBundleViewAccess() and treated as forbidden, so comment was never included.

The fix is in ApiUiContentEntityReferenceControllers::createBundleStub(). item.title: #3591130: Deleted (code) components can still be referenced by folders: dependency handling is missing
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +18/−0 · php +18
  • Discussion: #3591130 · 2 contributors · 9 comments
  • Followers: 4

Summary

When a Canvas component is renamed via the CLI, the operation is actually a delete followed by a create. Any Folder config entity that listed the old component in its items retained the stale name after the delete, because Canvas's dependency tracking did not know the connection existed. A later operation on that folder (such as a PATCH) would fail with a 422 "Unprocessable Content" error and a message like "The 'canvas.component.js.media-feature-grid' config does not exist." The fix adds proper config-dependency declarations to Folder so that Drupal's built-in dependency resolution removes deleted components from folder items automatically. Existing sites need to run database updates to recompute the previously missing dependencies.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: New post-update function resaves all Folder entities to compute previously missing config dependencies; run drush updb after updating.

Technical details

The root cause is that Folder never overrode calculateDependencies(). It inherited ConfigEntityBase::preDelete() and ConfigEntityBase::onDependencyRemoval() unchanged, but those methods can only act on dependencies that have already been declared. Because no dependencies were declared, deleting or renaming a JavaScriptComponent (or any other config entity stored in a folder) left the Folder's items array untouched. The fix in !1133 implements Folder::calculateDependencies() to register each item in items as a config dependency. Once those dependencies are present in the config graph, ConfigEntityBase::onDependencyRemoval() can fire and strip the deleted entry from items without any custom delete-hook logic. A post-update function (modeled on canvas_post_update_0002_intermediate_component_dependencies_in_patterns() and its companion UpdateIntermediateDependenciesUpdateTest) was added to resave all existing Folder entities so their dependency metadata is computed and stored. This MR (!1135) contains only the corresponding test in CanvasConfigEntityHttpApiTest, asserting that after an HTTP DELETE of a component, the folder's items list is empty. A related follow-up issue, #3591475, tracks the additional behavior of deleting the Folder itself when its last dependency is removed.

Upgrade

After updating the module, run database updates to recompute folder dependencies on existing sites:

drush updb
# or
vendor/bin/drush updb

Without this step, existing Folder config entities will continue to lack declared dependencies and the bug will persist for them even after the code update.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 20, 2026

Key contributors

  • bnjmnm (Acquia)
  • wim leers (Acquia)

Collaboration

wim leers identified the underlying cause in comment #5: because Folder never implemented calculateDependencies(), Drupal's config dependency system had no record of the folder-to-component relationship, making all the inherited removal machinery inert. This reframed the fix from a bespoke delete-hook approach to a standard dependency-declaration approach. He also flagged the need for a database update path for existing sites, and generated it using an AI tool in a single prompt for $1.73 and roughly nine minutes.

item.title: #3576837: Manage the global layout (aka regions) within Canvas Workbench
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 68 files, +3196/−509 · js +2827/−495 · mdx +140/−9 · php +92 · json +62/−3 · md +51/−2 · yml +24
  • Discussion: #3576837 · 5 contributors · 13 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Canvas Workbench and the Canvas CLI now treat global regions (header, footer, etc.) as first-class items alongside pages and content templates. Developers place region JSON specs in a regionsDir directory, run canvas pull --include-regions or canvas push --include-regions to two-way sync them with Drupal, and optionally add a src/layout.jsx file that wraps Workbench page and content template previews with the surrounding regions. If the layout file is absent, previews continue rendering without surrounding regions, so existing projects are unaffected until they opt in.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: canvas_oauth_post_update_0006_page_region_scope installs a new canvas:page_region OAuth scope gated by the administer page template permission.
  • New API: New regionsDir and layoutPath config keys in canvas.config.json; new --include-regions CLI flag for pull, push, and validate; new ApiService methods listRegions, getRegion, createRegion, updateRegion, deleteRegion targeting /canvas/api/v0/config/page_region; Region component exported from drupal-canvas@^0.4.0.

Technical details

Two new keys are added to canvas.config.json: regionsDir (default ./regions) and layoutPath (default ./src/layout.jsx). Region spec files in regionsDir use the same element tree JSON format as page specs. The filename (without extension) becomes the region machine name; the Drupal theme is implicit and resolved server-side from the default theme when pushing. Push semantics are full-sync: remote regions absent from the local regionsDir are deleted.

The ApiService class gains listRegions(), getRegion(), createRegion(), updateRegion(), and deleteRegion() methods, all targeting the /canvas/api/v0/config/page_region REST endpoint. The --include-regions / CANVAS_INCLUDE_REGIONS=true option is wired into the pull, push, and validate commands. A new createRegionsPullTask() function and push utilities (prepareRegions, pushRegions, collectRegionResults, validateRegions) parallel the existing page and content-template paths.

A new canvas:page_region OAuth scope is installed by canvas_oauth_post_update_0006_page_region_scope, gated by the administer page template permission. The canvas_oauth authentication provider now protects PageRegion config entities alongside ContentTemplate, BrandKit, and others.

The layout file must export a default React component accepting children. The Region component from drupal-canvas (now at ^0.4.0) slots in a region by machine name; regions with no matching spec file render as nothing, and a fallback prop can supply a placeholder during development.

Internally, the authored-element-utils module is consolidated into a new authored-elements module that exposes shared helpers (componentTreeToAuthoredElementMap, authoredElementMapToComponentTree, jsonRenderSpecToAuthoredElementMap) used by all three entity types. A new ConfigComponentTreePayload type and stripNullableKeysForConfigComponentTree() function handle the fact that config-entity component trees (regions, content templates) reject null values for parent_uuid, slot, and label, while page content entities tolerate them. The now-redundant authoredPropToServer() pass-through (which was only a no-op for pages/regions) is removed from the content-template utilities.

Upgrade

After running database updates, the new OAuth scope is available:

drush updb

To opt in to region sync, add to canvas.config.json:

{
  "regionsDir": "./regions",
  "layoutPath": "./src/layout.jsx"
}

Create region specs in regions/:

// regions/header.json
{
  "status": true,
  "elements": {
    "header": {
      "type": "js.header",
      "props": { "darkVariant": true },
      "slots": { "branding": ["header-logo"] }
    },
    "header-logo": {
      "type": "js.logo",
      "props": { "linkToFrontPage": true }
    }
  }
}

Create src/layout.jsx to wrap Workbench previews with regions:

import { Region } from 'drupal-canvas';

export default function Layout({ children }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Region name="header" />
      <main>{children}</main>
      <Region name="footer" />
    </>
  );
}

Pull or push regions with the new flag:

npx canvas pull --include-regions
npx canvas push --include-regions

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 3, 2026

Key contributors

  • wotnak (Smartbees)
  • balintbrews (Acquia)
  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • effulgentsia (Acquia)
  • rikki_iki
  • lauriii (Acquia)

Collaboration

The design discussion shaped the final approach significantly. effulgentsia proposed three options for how to surface regions in Workbench, and in comment #16522896 described a conversation with rikki_iki in which she suggested Option 2 (regions shown as part of page previews rather than in isolation) and specifically proposed using React Router concepts — a layout with an outlet — rather than Drupal's region terminology in the local codebase. wotnak pushed back in comment #16582626, arguing that purely using an outlet without a local concept of regions would make two-way CLI sync difficult, and proposed the hybrid approach that landed: local region JSON specs that sync like pages, combined with a local layout.jsx for Workbench rendering. wim leers flagged in comment #16584111 that making PageRegion implement CanvasHttpApiEligibleConfigEntityInterface carried significant security implications and requested it be extracted to a separate blocking issue, which became #3589801.

item.title: #3556101: [11.3.x] Semi-coupled engine not compatible with Drupal 11.x
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +321/−325 · php +315/−322 · yml +6/−3
  • Discussion: #3556101 · 6 contributors · 13 comments
  • Followers: 9

Summary

Canvas's semi_coupled theme engine became incompatible with Drupal 11.3.x after core issue #1685492 converted theme engines from hook-based .engine files into tagged services. Any Canvas page on an 11.3.x site threw a 500 error with the message Service "semi_coupled" not found: the container inside "Drupal\Core\Theme\ThemeManager" is a smaller service locator that only knows about the "twig" service. This issue proposed converting the engine to comply with the new service-based API. It was ultimately closed as fixed when #3555062 removed the semi-coupled theme engine from Canvas entirely, making Canvas compatible with both 11.2.x and 11.3.x without needing the engine approach at all.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause is that Drupal 11.3.x (core #1685492) requires theme engines to be registered as tagged services implementing ThemeEngineInterface rather than as standalone .engine files providing procedural hooks (hook_extension(), hook_theme(), hook_render_template()). The old semi_coupled.engine file and its accompanying semi_coupled.info.yml (of type theme_engine) were incompatible with this model.

MR !296 proposes the intermediate fix: move all engine logic from procedural functions into a SemiCoupledEngine class implementing ThemeEngineInterface, and register it in canvas.services.yml with tags: [{name: theme_engine, engine_name: semi_coupled}]. The methods theme() and renderTemplate() map directly to the old semi_coupled_theme() and semi_coupled_render_template() hooks; the helper functions _semi_coupled_collect_props(), _semi_coupled_build_html_tag(), _semi_coupled_get_variable(), _semi_coupled_snake_case(), and _semi_coupled_kebab_case() become private methods on the class.

This MR was not merged. The actual fix arrived via #3555062, which removed the semi_coupled theme engine from Canvas entirely and improved React embedding without relying on a custom engine, resolving the 11.3.x incompatibility in a way that also kept 11.2.x working.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 5, 2025

Collaboration

alexpott identified a parallel fix in core (#3556130, "ThemeEngine BC layer is broken - ServiceLocator != Container") immediately after the issue was filed, which briefly raised the question of whether the Canvas side needed changing at all. wim leers and penyaskito clarified that Canvas targets 11.2.x as its minimum and would not require 11.3.x for 1.0, so the issue was postponed until the minimum version bumped. phenaproxima pointed out that landing #3555062 (removing the engine) would close this issue as outdated without needing the tagged-service migration at all, and that is ultimately what happened.

item.title: #3555487: default-relative-url may crash with JSON storage
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3555487 · 2 contributors · 3 comments
  • Followers: 3

Summary

On MySQL 8.0, which stores JSON natively rather than as a string, the Canvas module can crash with a 500 error when rendering pages that use default prop values for image or video components. This caused the Byte demo home page of Drupal CMS 2.0 to fail on MySQL 8.0. The fix landed in the related issue #3550165.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The crash originates in Drupal\canvas\PropSource\DefaultRelativeUrlPropSource, which compares a stored JSON schema against a minimal expected shape using ksort() before an equality check. That one-level sort does not recurse into nested properties keys, so when MySQL 8.0's native JSON type returns property keys in a different order than MariaDB's string-encoded JSON, the comparison fails and an exception is thrown. Versions of MariaDB that DDEV defaults to store JSON as strings, preserving insertion order and masking the bug; MySQL 8.0 does not, exposing it. The fix, applied in #3550165, adds a second pass of ksort() over each entry inside properties for both the stored schema and the minimal schema before the equality check.

item.title: #3549124: Confirm overriding local global CSS file with the download command
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3549124 · 1 contributor · 2 comments
  • Followers: 2

Summary

The Canvas CLI tool previously fetched global.css from Canvas silently in the background during build and upload, and the download command would overwrite the local global.css without warning. This issue, resolved via #3560957, introduces explicit control over global CSS syncing. The download and upload commands now list "Global CSS" as a selectable option in interactive mode (pre-selected by default). The build command switches to a local-first strategy: it reads the local global.css when it exists instead of always pulling from the remote API. New --skip-css and --css-only flags for both download and upload give non-interactive and CI/CD users precise control over whether and what CSS is transferred.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New --skip-css and --css-only flags on the download and upload CLI commands; getGlobalCss() and downloadGlobalCssInBackground() utility functions added to build-tailwind.ts

Technical details

The core change is a getGlobalCss(useLocal: boolean = true) function added to build-tailwind.ts. When useLocal is true and a local global.css exists under the configured CANVAS_COMPONENT_DIR, it is read from disk; otherwise the function falls back to downloadGlobalCssInBackground(), which calls apiService.getGlobalAssetLibrary() without touching the local file. Both buildComponent() in build.ts and buildTailwindForComponents() in build-tailwind.ts now accept a useLocalGlobalCss parameter (default true) and pass it through to getGlobalCss, replacing their previous direct calls to apiService.getGlobalAssetLibrary() for CSS.

The component-selector.ts module gains a GLOBAL_CSS_SELECTOR sentinel string and a determineGlobalCssSelection() helper. Both selectLocalComponents() and selectRemoteComponents() return an includeGlobalCss boolean in their result types (LocalSelectorResult and RemoteSelectorResult). In interactive mode, a "Global CSS" option is inserted immediately after "All components" and pre-selected when globalCssDefault is true. The --css-only path short-circuits component discovery entirely and returns an empty component list with includeGlobalCss: true.

The download command now fetches components and global CSS in parallel via Promise.all (unless --css-only is set, in which case only CSS is fetched), and writes the local global.css only when includeGlobalCss is true. The upload command skips the global CSS upload when includeGlobalCss is false, and passes includeGlobalCss through getBuildAndUploadResults to control which CSS source is used for the Tailwind build. An inline @todo workaround that re-fetched the existing css.original from the API before every upload (to avoid overwriting it with an empty value) was removed, since getGlobalCss() now provides the correct local source.

Upgrade

CLI users and CI/CD scripts that call npx canvas build, npx canvas download, or npx canvas upload should note the behavior changes:

  • build and upload now use the local global.css by default instead of fetching CSS from Canvas on every run. Ensure your local global.css is up to date before building.
  • download now includes global CSS in the download by default. Use --skip-css to preserve the old skip behavior.
  • New flags for download and upload:
# Skip global CSS during download or upload
npx canvas download --all --skip-css
npx canvas upload --all --skip-css

# Transfer only global CSS, skip components
npx canvas download --css-only
npx canvas upload --css-only
  • --skip-css and --css-only cannot be combined; doing so throws an error.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 27, 2025

Collaboration

The design was shaped by a focused exchange between balintbrews and lauriii early in the thread. lauriii questioned whether silently compiling with the remote CSS when a user skips the global CSS upload would produce confusing "side effects," particularly in multi-user environments where one person edits via CLI and another edits in the browser code editor. In response, balintbrews updated the issue summary to adopt lauriii's preferred behavior: when global CSS upload is skipped, the build falls back to fetching the remote CSS in the background without touching the local file, making any differences in compiled output an explicit consequence of the user's choice rather than a hidden surprise.

item.title: #3544517: Support SVG images
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3544517 · 2 contributors · 4 comments
  • Followers: 3

Summary

Experience Builder (canvas) previously validated image prop URLs by matching file extensions with a hardcoded regex that only permitted PNG, GIF, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, and AVIF. This excluded SVG and any other image format. The fix replaces that approach with the JSON Schema contentMediaType: image/* annotation, allowing any image MIME type. The same change applies to video props, which previously only allowed MP4. As a side effect, the system now properly maps image string props to the image field type rather than a plain string field type, which means image props in generated field-based UX components are backed by an image field with the image_image widget instead of a plain text field.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: JSON schema definitions image-uri and stream-wrapper-image-uri replace extension-regex pattern with contentMediaType: image/* and a simplified URL pattern; image and video prop shapes now map to field type image with widget image_image instead of string.

Technical details

The old json-schema-definitions://experience_builder.module/image-uri and stream-wrapper-image-uri definitions carried pattern regexes that explicitly enumerated case-insensitive extensions. Those are replaced with contentMediaType: image/* plus a simplified URL-structure pattern. The video prop definition similarly moves from an MP4-only extension regex to contentMediaType: video/*.

On the matching side, JsonSchemaFieldInstanceMatcher previously called buildCaseInsensitiveExtensionRegex() to synthesise extension-based Regex constraints for file URI field properties. That method is removed. Instead, a new fileExtensionsToTargetContentMediaType() helper uses the file.mime_type.guesser.extension service to map a media type's allowed extensions to their wildcard MIME category (e.g. ["jpg","png","svg"] → "image/*"), and attaches the new UriTargetMediaTypeConstraint instead.

UriTargetMediaTypeConstraint is a no-op validation constraint (modelled on Drupal core's FullyValidatable) whose only role is to carry MIME type semantics on a data definition, enabling the shape-matching logic in mediaLibraryStoragePropShapeAlter and JsonSchemaStringFormat::computeStorablePropShape() to recognise image and video URI props and wire them to the image field type with the image_image widget.

Supporting changes: DataTypeShapeRequirement and DataTypeShapeRequirements now implement \IteratorAggregate, letting JsonSchemaType spread either type uniformly. StorablePropShape::fieldTypeProp and CandidateStorablePropShape::fieldTypeProp now accept ReferenceFieldTypePropExpression in addition to FieldTypePropExpression|FieldTypeObjectPropsExpression. JsonSchemaType::patternToPcre() extracts the pattern-to-PCRE conversion that was previously inlined. The ordering of format vs pattern cases in JsonSchemaType::computeStorablePropShape() was corrected so that format takes precedence when both are present.

Upgrade

SDC prop schemas for image URLs must replace the old extension regex with contentMediaType and a URL-structure pattern:

# Before
src:
  type: string
  format: uri-reference
  pattern: '^(/|https?://)?.*\.([Pp][Nn][Gg]|[Gg][Ii][Ff]|[Jj][Pp][Gg]|[Jj][Pp][Ee][Gg]|[Ww][Ee][Bb][Pp]|[Aa][Vv][Ii][Ff])(\?.*)?(#.*)?$'

# After — or use $ref: json-schema-definitions://experience_builder.module/image-uri
src:
  type: string
  format: uri-reference
  contentMediaType: image/*
  pattern: '^(/|https?://)?(?!.*\://)[^\s]+$'

Stream-wrapper image URIs:

# Before
src:
  type: string
  format: uri
  pattern: '^(?!https?://)[\w\-]+://.*\.([Pp][Nn][Gg]|...)(\?.*)?(#.*)?$'

# After — or use $ref: json-schema-definitions://experience_builder.module/stream-wrapper-image-uri
src:
  type: string
  format: uri
  contentMediaType: image/*
  pattern: '^(?!https?://)[\w\-]+://'

Video URL props follow the same pattern with contentMediaType: video/*.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 3, 2025

Key contributors

  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • wim leers (Acquia)

Collaboration

wim leers pointed out in the issue thread that the regex had already been removed in commit 9048ab8 as part of a broader refactor (with a linked change record at drupal.org/node/3542579), and asked larowlan to retest against HEAD. larowlan confirmed the issue was resolved after doing so.

Selecting an item navigates to /template/:entityType/:bundle/:viewMode/:previewEntityId.

A new route /template/:entityType/:bundle/:viewMode (without previewEntityId) is registered alongside the existing :previewEntityId route. It renders the new TemplateRoot component, which on mount queries useGetContentTemplatesQuery and immediately redirects (with replace) to the suggested entity if one is available. When none is found, it renders the no-content notice; the "Add new" button constructs a URL as {baseUrl}{entityType}/add/{bundle} using getBaseUrl().

PageInfo gains template-route awareness: it shows a FileIcon and a caption of the form {bundleLabel} - {viewModeLabel} template, resolved by looking up bundle and view mode labels from the existing useGetContentTemplatesQuery response.

New types PreviewContentEntity and PreviewContentEntitiesResponse are added in the services file, and PreviewContentEntities is registered as a new RTK cache tag. The TemplateListItem link fallback is also corrected from 0 to an empty string for cases where suggestedPreviewEntityId is absent.
